name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ -7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=5$ and ${y}_{2}=33.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 33\end{aligned}].$

Question 5
?

Consider the matrix L and the vector b, given by

L=[10−71],b=[5−2].

If A=LU is the LU factorization of some 2×2 matrix A, find the vector y such that

{Ly=bUx=y is equivalent to Ax=b.

a
y=[5−7]
b
y=[53]
c
y=[1−7]
d
y=[533]
e
y=[15]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that since A=LU, we can write

Ax=b⟹(LU)⏟Ax=b.

Now, setting Ux=y, we obtain

L(Ux)⏟y=b⟹{Ly=bUx=y.

We now solve Ly=b. Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

[10−71][y1y2]=[5−2]. This gives the system of equations {y1=5−7y1+y2=−2. The solution to this system is y1=5 and y2=33.

Therefore, y=[533].
